headline: Tabled letter to Governor Scott requesting state support for Church Street Marketplace until September 30.
summary: The Commission reviewed holiday season plans, including the Santa Parade and Tree Lighting on 11/27, new marketing programs, and transportation ideas for downtown. Commissioners discussed a draft letter to Governor Scott about support for the Marketplace and voted to table it until September 30 for further changes. Staff gave Treasurer's, Director's, and Chair's reports covering budget status, safety initiatives, foot traffic data, and vacancies.
decisions: Tabled the letter to Governor Scott requesting support for the Marketplace until September 30, with one abstention.

decision_evidence.quote: Proposition to table letter to the Governor until 9/30 ... Vote: Passes (Abstention by L.Magoon)

Church Street Marketplace Commission 
Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 9:00am. 
Hybrid Meeting via Zoom and in City Hall’s Sharon Bushor Conference Room 
 
 
Staff Present: Commissioners Present:  
☒ Kara Alnasrawi 
☒ Sam McGinnis  
☒ Jessica Dudley 
☒ Aida Washburn

☒ Becky Holt

☒ Marykate Moore (Online)

Public Attendance: No Attendance  
 
 
 
1. Agenda  
Call to Order: 9:04am 
Changes to Agenda: None 
 
2. Adopt Minutes  
 
1. Vote passed Unanimously 9:05am 
 
3. Public Forum  
 
1. There was no public attendance and no comments were made  
 
4. Commissioner’s Items  
 
1. C.Haessly recommended checking out Samba House! And the City’s new AI policy.  
2. E.Monsen noted that college students have returned to town.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes   
 
 
5. Holiday Preview 9:10am 
 
1. S.McGinnis and J.Dudley lead the presentation covering the upcoming holiday season. 
2. Santa Parade and Tree Lighting on 11/27 
3. Family Programming, this year three distinct modes of communication to improve 
communication. S.McGinnis continued to outline events and new additions for the season.  
4. J.Dudley spoke to advertising and marketing. Print ads, TV ads, Digital ads and Radio ads 
5. S.McGinnis and J.Dudley spoke to other community initiatives. Burlington after 5, new 
website that will show what businesses will be open after 5pm during the holiday season.  
6. Shop Local get Rewarded, new program. L.Magoon and S.Beal asked questions about the 
new program.  
7. All of the winter programming to be wrapped into Winter in the City; this will work the 
same way Summer in the City worked.  
8. Questions: 
a. S.Beal, asked for physical material to encourage business to business support. 
M.Bouchett voiced support for in-person marketing. 
b. E.Monsen said that, “digital receipts would be better than paper”. Also spoke to 
concerns about using QR codes for votes and how might we improve voting 
accuracy. S.Beal responded, asked if there needed to be a “winner” or if there are 
other ways to encourage participation. E.Monsen voiced support for “Best in 
Category” approach. 
c. L.Magoon suggested that if stores knew what each other offered, this could 
increase business. S.Beal commented that a map might help with this. K.Alnasrawi 
voiced that there has been unwillingness in the past by businesses to participate 
in such a map. C.Haessly suggested that a digital kiosk or app/website might 
work well for this. 
d. S.Beal asked if a holiday trolley, bus or shuttle service from UVM might 
encourage people who are afraid to park downtown. “Holiday Express” style . 
e. Holiday conversation evolved into broader conversation about unique downtown 
transportation in general. 
 
 
6. Letter to Governor Scott Requesting Support for the Marketplace 
 
1. L.Magoon spoke with concerned constituents and the idea to send a letter to the 
governor was proposed. Pulling from the feedback from the community, Linda drafted a 
letter. 
2. C.Haessly spoke to what he has heard from outside Burlington that the current problems 
were in part created by the decisions made by the City and that we have a responsibility 
to fix these issues before or in conjunction with state support. Chris suggested changes to 
language in the letter to reframe the points made.  
3. S.Beal, “Burlington’s unhoused and drug issues are Vermont’s unhoused and drug issues” 
Stated that we need to make this clear in the letter.  
4. S.Beal continued to comment on the proposed 100-bed shelter and the need to push for 
this. B.Holt added that they do not believe that a 100 bed shelter is a good idea, too many 
people in one location. They also stated that direct communication with state police and 
BPD needs to happen to improve enforcement downtown. 
5. B.Holt echoed what S.Beal has said earlier, that “these issues are not just Burlington 
issues but are Chittenden county issues”.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes   
 
 
6. K.Alnasrawi responded to B.Holt, CVOEO indicated that they would be unable to run 
multiple separate shelters. Acknowledged that a shelter of this size is not the current 
standard of care but is needed for the current emergency. Continued to speak to state 
police presence and how they are not allowed to respond to calls for service or enforce 
ordinance such as open container etc. 
7. Conversation turned back to the letter and what should be included. Timetable, election 
year and tone of letter all being considered by all commissioners. C.Haessly identified 
two aspects of the letter starting a real dialog with the state and request of resources for 
the city. Discussion continued and a motion to table the letter was posed.  
 
10:20am 
Action: Proposition to table letter to the Governor until 9/30  
Motion by: C.Haessly 
Seconded by: S.Beal 
Vote: Passes (Abstention by L.Magoon) 
 
Vote to be taken on September 30th. The letter to be circulated and changed made prior to 
the meeting and subsequent vote.  
 
  
7. Reports 10:22am 
 
1. Treasurer’s Report  
• M.Bouchett gave the report in the absence of a Treasurer. 11% into budget year 
and 11% of budget spent.  
 
2. Director’s Report  
• S.McGinnis gave report on Mainstreet America. Burlington was the case study for 
this workshop. S.McGinnis continues to work with the MSA team to develop 
strategies, etc. Overarching theme was safety and security. Very positive 
experience for all in this workshop. 
• Discussed Mayor’s meeting with Burlington businesses last month. Primary focus 
of this meeting was safety and security.  
• Discussed Hot Spots group, made up of members of each city department 
focused on specific areas causing issues throughout the city. These include, road 
closures, city hall park disturbances, etc.  
• Spoke to second round of police chief interviews moving forward.  
• Gave recap of upcoming CSM events.  
• Additional bollards have been ordered.  
• No updates on CSM vacancies.  
 
3. Chair’s Report  
• M.Bouchett announced the departure of J.Dudley to the commission.  
• Spoke to his work with S.McGinnis into CSM foot traffic data. Goal to set 
benchmark and project to be continued into the future.  
• Discussed wayfinding with S.McGinnis. Looking into digital boards for CSM  
• Gave update on vacancy of Treasurer seat. No applicants have yet to be 
identified.
Burlington Planning Commission Minutes   
 
 
 
8. Adjournment 
Action: Motion to Adjourn  
Time of Adjournment: 10:43am 
Motion by: C.Haessly 
Seconded by: S.Beal 
Vote: Unanimous
